item.title: Women's advocacy groups respond to Caitlin Clark's answer on demonstrations at Fever games
item.description: Multiple groups react to Caitlin Clark's response about trans athletes in women's sports, with some expressing disappointment in her neutral stance.
item.content:encoded:
Caitlin Clark's answer to a question about the WNBA's convergence with the "Save Women's Sports" movement became a point of internal debate within the movement and her fan base in recent days.

Dave Portnoy and Megyn Kelly, two known Clark supporters, even went at it on X about it.

Clark was asked Sunday about the WNBA's ongoing controversy related to demonstrations outside of Indiana Fever games. Her teammate Sophie Cunningham voiced her support for protecting women's sports from biological males in late July, and rallies in support of Cunningham have followed the Fever to their last three games. Counterprotests have also appeared outside each of the last three games.

WNBA SUDDENLY WANTS TO STICK TO BASKETBALL AFTER YEARS OF MAKING POLITICS PART OF THE PRODUCT

Clark did not reveal her stance on the issue when she answered, but deferred to the governing bodies and leagues that oversee women's sports.

"I think, for us, it's not really a discussion we really have in our locker room," Clark answered. "I think it's for leagues and the governing bodies to work with their athletes to find solutions. Our focus is on basketball. That's what we talk about and how we can get wins, and, obviously, we didn't do that tonight. So we need to find an area to improve in that way."

Clark then declined a related follow-up question, saying "I just answered for you."

Multiple advocacy groups leading the "Save Women's Sports" movement have addressed Clark's answer in statements to Fox News Digital.

Some of the groups appeared to defend Clark.

"Female athletes should never be forced to 'pick a side' to defend their right to the same opportunities afforded to men or be pressured to surrender that right in the middle of their careers. Yet because sport leaders have failed to adopt clear, fair policies, players are left carrying that burden themselves, creating unnecessary conflict among teammates, friends, and competitors," ICONS co-founder Marshi Smith told Fox News Digital.

SJSU VOLLEYBALL SCANDAL PROBE FINDS TEAM ALLEGEDLY RECRUITED MALE FOR ADVANTAGE WITHOUT TELLING FEMALE PLAYERS

"We saw the devastating toll of this during the Mountain West volleyball controversy, where women were placed in the impossible position of choosing between standing up for what they believed was fair or forfeiting games at the expense of their teams.

"The resulting tension fractured relationships and divided women’s teams. That division was not created by the athletes. It was the product of institutional failure. Women’s leagues should be for women. It is the responsibility of sport leaders, not individual players, to protect the integrity of women’s competition so athletes can focus on what they came to do: compete. But when policymakers fail women, courage falls to the athletes. History has always revealed the difference between the timid and the bold, between those captive to ideology and those willing to stand for what is right."

"Everyone should be able to make the point that a women's league should be for women. This shouldn't be hard. It’s understandable that Caitlin Clark wants to dodge this question because the leadership of her league has been so embarrassing in their response," Independent Women President Carrie Lukas told Fox News Digital.

"That's a disservice to every female professional basketball player and every young girl who hopes to play in the future. Of course, men shouldn't be allowed in women's basketball. Full stop. You can support both equality and protecting women's sports for females only. That's why the women's basketball league exists."

THESE FEMALE ATHLETES NEED TO SPEAK UP ABOUT KEEPING WOMEN'S SPORTS FOR WOMEN, LIKE SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM DID

"Caitlin Clark had an opportunity to stand up for women and girls, and she chose not to. This isn't a question that should be punted or treated as someone else's responsibility. Female athletes deserve leaders and role models willing to say what the science, common sense, and now the U.S. Supreme Court have recognized: sex matters in sports," Independent Women’s Law Center senior legal counsel Beth Parlato told Fox News Digital.

"Protecting women's sports isn't controversial; it is essential to preserving fairness, safety, and equal athletic opportunity for female athletes. More athletes need to take a stand like Sophie Cunningham has and have the courage to speak clearly in defense of the very category that made their own success possible."

"Athletes like Sophie Cunningham who are standing up for women and girls to have fair competition are exceptional and courageous. We hope that Clark and every other WNBA player will stand up in support of female athletes. But ultimately, the WNBA and other sports governing bodies must facilitate fair and safe competitions so their athletes can focus on competing. The WNBA should immediately adopt a policy that establishes only biological women can play basketball in the league. Does the WNBA stand for fairness in women’s sports or not?" Concerned Women for America CEO and President Penny Nance told Fox News Digital.

"Women in the public eye have a responsibility to set an example for the young girls watching them, and that starts with standing up for the fundamentals of basic biology. It should never be difficult to defend common sense, and it should never be controversial to protect young girls. Every woman with a platform has a choice: stand up for the next generation of girls, or stay silent while their opportunities, their privacy, and their safety are taken away. Parents across America know where Moms for Liberty stands, and we will never back down." Moms for Liberty CEO and Co-Founder of Moms for Liberty Tina Descovich told Fox News Digital.

item.title: Hasan Piker, Abdul El-Sayed mock James Carville threatening to leave Democrats and 'sweetening the deal'
item.description: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker and Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed mocked strategist James Carville's threat to leave the Democratic Party.
item.content:encoded:
Far-left Twitch streamer Hasan Piker and Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed mocked the idea of longtime Democrats like James Carville leaving the party because of them on Monday.

Ahead of the Democratic primary on Tuesday, Piker spoke with El-Sayed in a video for his channel. The two began by discussing the "full-on freakout" caused by Piker choosing to campaign for El-Sayed, leading to people like Carville attacking their own party.

"Now James Carville is talking about leaving the party," Piker said. "We got [Pennsylvania Sen.] John Fetterman, James Carville fantasizing about leaving the party. I'm like, you're sweetening the deal. That was really interesting."

HASAN PIKER DRAWS FRESH SCRUTINY AFTER FRAMING NEWSPAPER COVERING 9/11 ATTACKS IN STREAM BACKGROUND

Piker was referring to comments made by Carville on Fox News' "The Sunday Briefing" regarding Piker's rise in prominence within the Democratic Party as he campaigned for socialist candidates.

"I can't sit here and tell you for certain how this is going to turn out, but the one thing I can tell you for certain, Hasan Piker and James Carville are not going to be in the same political party. One of us is going to leave. It might even be me," Carville told Fox News, adding that an "overwhelming majority" of Democrats agreed with him.

El-Sayed was similarly dismissive of Carville's comments, suggesting Carville himself was responsible for party shifts during the Clinton administration.

CARVILLE SAYS ONE DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST'S 'LUNACY OF THE HIGHEST LEVEL' POLICY COULD HAUNT SWING-STATE DEMS

"That was really interesting. Like our party, if you look at what happened with [President Donald] Trump, you had a whole bunch of center-right people realize that they had no home in the party that they destroyed. And then they all came to our party and tried to tell us what our party ought to be. And then you think about like James Carville, I'm like, bro, you architected the complete right-wing ascent to neoliberalism in '96," El-Sayed said.

Piker added, "This state is a swing state because of the machinations of the Clinton era of politics."

Fox News Digital reached out to Carville for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

HASAN PIKER'S DEFENSE OF HAMAS HAVING 'RIGHT TO RESIST MILITARILY' DRAWS CONDEMNATION FROM HUMAN RIGHTS GROUPS

Piker drew widespread criticism for making several controversial statements, including that America "deserved" 9/11 and that Hamas was "a thousand times better" than Israel.

Despite his comments, El-Sayed has repeatedly defended campaigning with Piker.

item.title: Beloved NC gas station clerk allegedly killed by registered sex offender after vanishing from home: deputies
item.description: Robin Doyle, 58, vanished from her Hickory, North Carolina, home before registered sex offender Leroy Allen Loper was charged with her felony murder.
item.content:encoded:
A beloved North Carolina gas station clerk was killed by a registered sex offender after vanishing from her home, deputies say.

Robin Doyle, 58, was reported missing on July 28 after she was last seen the previous day by a family member. When deputies showed up to her home in Hickory, North Carolina, she wasn't there, according to the Catawba County Sheriff's Office.

After Doyle was found dead on Friday in a wooded area of northeastern Catawba County, 54-year-old Leroy Allen Loper was arrested on charges of felony murder, first-degree kidnapping and concealment of death.

Loper is a registered sex offender with previous felony convictions for first-degree kidnapping and second-degree forcible sexual offense, officials added.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

He is being held at the Catawba County Detention Facility with no bond.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

"We are deeply saddened for Robin Doyle's family as they continue to endure an unimaginable loss. While today's charges mark a significant step in this investigation, they cannot undo the pain this family has suffered. The acts in this case represent pure evil, and those responsible will be held fully accountable under the law. This investigation remains active, and we will continue pursuing every fact until justice is fully served," Catawba County Sheriff Don Brown said.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Those who knew Doyle described her to WBTV as a kind woman who was a fixture behind the counter at the gas station where she worked.

GOT A TIP?

"She was one of the sweetest, most generous, kindhearted, amazing people you’ll ever meet in your life," said Corban Worley. "Her car is not here nor her warm smile, welcoming when you came into the store."

At the Propst Superette, where Doyle worked, a tribute on the store read, "Robin, the world wasn’t ready for you to leave, but heaven needed you home."

item.title: Carrie Underwood is back for SNF, Angel Reese celebrates Barbie Night & NFL WAGs are training-camp ready
item.description: Carrie Underwood returns for her 14th season performing the "Sunday Night Football" theme, while NFL WAGs send husbands off to training camp.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Happy to report I am back in the beautiful state of Tennessee.

The husband, dog and I had a nice time on our pilgrimage to the Great White North, but I am happy to be back in my own cozy home, sleeping on my own elite mattress and caring for my own little house plants.

And there's much to do now that I'm back.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

We have some exciting things coming up in OutKick Outdoors. No spoilers, but if you're into hunting, fishing, hiking, camping or even just drinking beer on patios, you should definitely be following us on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube.

Ain't too proud for a shameless plug, baby.

But that's enough of that for now. We've got some Nightcaps to do.

There's an old saying that goes, "If it ain't broke, don't fix it."

And that's exactly why NBC invited back Carrie Underwood to perform the theme song ahead of Sunday Night Football — for the 14th season in a row.

I mean, who else are you gonna get? That lady from the Women’s Pro Baseball League?

It's like they pulled three random drunk women out of a crowd and handed them microphones.

Point is, Carrie Underwood is a crowd pleaser. So come September, she and her glorious legs (I say that as an entirely straight woman) will — once again — bless our TV screens before we watch someone play against the Dallas Cowboys or Kansas City Chiefs.

Seriously, those teams make three SNF appearances each this season. You know who doesn't get any Carrie Underwood games? The Dolphins, Jets and Raiders.

Womp.

Not that I blame the schedule-makers there. I'm a Dolphins fan, and even I believe no one should be subjected to that dumpster fire in prime time.

Fun game of would you rather: three hours of Miami Dolphins football or the Martha Reeves national anthem on repeat?

Faced with that option, it almost makes Malik Washington to Jalen Tolbert sound exhilarating.

Anyway, Carrie's ready. I'm ready. You're ready. Let's get to September already.

You know who else is ready for football season? The NFL WAGs, who are pushing their boyfriends and husbands out of the house for a few weeks of uninterrupted quiet time during training camp.

Back when I worked for the Titans, anyone with fewer than three seasons (I think that was the cutoff) in the league had to stay at the Millennium Maxwell House. What a s— hole that was. It sounds fancy, but I promise: certified s— hole.

One time one of our running backs got bed bugs there, and the whole place had to be fumigated. Then, all the players lined up in a queue of shame to dump all of their worldly belongings into the laundry bin at the facility.

I was careful not to touch anything in the locker room that week. No creepy crawlies in my house, thank you.

I don't know how the Titans do training camp now, but I hope — for the players' sake — they found nicer accommodations. Or let them live at home.

Here's Drew Allar's girlfriend stocking him up with all the snacks he'll need to back up Aaron Rodgers.

Here's Isaiah Likely's wife, Melanie, sending him off in style.

Here's Myles Garrett's girlfriend — Olympic snowboarder Chloe Kim — passive aggressively wishing herself a happy National Girlfriends Day since Myles apparently forgot to.

To be fair, he's trying to learn a whole new playbook out there in LA. Also, no sane person on planet earth knows when National Girlfriend Day is.

And finally, here's Jaxson Dart's girlfriend, Marissa Ayers, who has no time to care about football right now. Because it's summer, and she's in Oahu.

This is probably no news to you. Because I'm sure you've had it in your calendar for months. But the Atlanta Dream held a Barbie theme night for Angel Reese.

It was either to celebrate the release of her special edition Barbie Doll or her Barbie pink signature Reebok shoes. Or both, I don't know.

Say what you want about the woman, but she is printing money.

Angel said this Barbie collaboration means a lot to her because when she was growing up, there weren't a lot of dolls who "looked like her" and hooped like her.

Of course, she's insinuating there weren't Black dolls. Or Black dolls who played basketball. Which is just categorically false. I'm older than Angel Reese (by more than a couple years), and dolls of all skin colors were readily available when I was a kid.

ANGEL REESE GOT A BARBIE DOLL, SIGNATURE SHOE AND WNBA THEME NIGHT, THEN PLAYED VICTIM AGAIN

As a user on Twitter / X pointed out today, Christie, Barbie's Black friend, entered Barbie’s world in 1968. The first official Black Barbie arrived in 1980. And in 1998, four years before Reese was born, Mattel was already selling Black basketball-playing Barbie dolls in authentic NBA uniforms.

If you ask me (and no one did), the real injustice is the shortage of brunette Barbies. For much of my childhood, I had to settle for Barbie's less popular friend Teresa. Where is my representation?! Where is my theme night?!

I'm in the weeds. Good for Angel and her doll and her signature shoe, I guess.

Apparently, Barbie Night was a real star-studded event at State Farm Arena — with celebrities like Flo Milli, Dess Dior and Chaylyn, the OMG Girlz, Saucy Santana and Mariah the Scientist (who I'm almost certain is not a real scientist) all in the building.

Look, I know I live three hours from Atlanta, but I honestly could not tell you who a single one of those people are — aside from Michael Harris, who plays for the Braves.

I'm glad they had a nice time, though.

Football season is around the corner, which means so is your fantasy draft.

And you better take it seriously or else you might end up forced to take the last-place punishment.

We've heard all the popular ones:

And then, there's this:

As someone who used to compete in bodybuilding shows, I can promise you that standing up on stage — nearly naked with an ungodly spray tan — and performing a posing routine is one of the more terrifying and humbling things you'll ever do in your lifetime.

Or never do, if you're smart.

And don't even get me started on the intense cardio, training and dieting you have to do for months ahead of time in order to look like you belong. Alternatively, I guess you can just say "f— it," trot on out there, and shamelesslystrut what the good Lord gave you. Like this guy did.

So is this the worst fantasy football punishment ever? Or can you top it?

Let me know.

item.title: Alarming missile report draws forceful response from Trump as Iran war tests America’s arsenal
item.description: A report says the Army has burned through virtually all ATACMS and PrSM stocks during the Iran conflict, raising fears about future crises.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration is rejecting concerns that the war with Iran has left the U.S. low on some of its most advanced long-range missiles, after a report found the Army burned through "virtually all" of its stocks of two of its primary long-range precision weapons.

The Army has used "virtually all" of its inventories of Army Tactical Missile Systems (ATACMS) and Precision Strike Missiles (PrSM) during the five-month conflict with Iran, Reuters, citing people familiar with internal U.S. military data, reported Tuesday. Officials fear the drawdown could complicate the military's ability to respond to future crises involving adversaries such as China and Russia, according to the report.

The White House disputed any suggestion the U.S. military lacks the weapons needed to carry out its missions.

WEAPONS STOCKPILE SHORTAGES IMPACTING MILITARY STRATEGY IN THE MIDEAST

"We have far more munitions than anyone in the world, and far more than we need, despite the fact that an unprecedented amount was given away by Crooked Joe Biden and the Biden Administration to Ukraine and Europe at no cost, in one of many of their extremely dumb moves," President Donald Trump said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital.

"Our defense companies are, at this moment, making more munitions than they have ever made before, in addition to expanding their plants and equipment at record levels. And as we build up, we will start issuing more to our allies in Europe and elsewhere."

If accurate, the report underscores a longstanding Pentagon concern: America's most sophisticated precision weapons can be expended in months but often take years to replace.

Reuters also reported that the conflict significantly reduced inventories of Patriot and THAAD missile interceptors, along with Tomahawk cruise missiles, though the Pentagon has maintained the U.S. military retains the capabilities needed to carry out operations worldwide.

HEGSETH DISMISSES ‘FOOLISH’ US STOCKPILE CONCERNS AS IRAN CONFLICT TESTS MUNITIONS

Exact U.S. weapons stockpile figures remain classified for national security reasons.

The Pentagon also pushed back on the reporting. "America’s military is the most powerful in the world and has everything it needs to execute at the time and place of the President’s choosing. We have executed multiple successful operations across combatant commands while ensuring the U.S. military possesses a deep arsenal of capabilities to protect our people and our interests," chief spokesman Sean Parnell said in a statement.

Independent analysts have also warned that months of combat have strained U.S. inventories of high-end munitions. The Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated last week that the U.S. had expended roughly 65% of its Patriot interceptor stockpile and that inventories of THAAD interceptors had fallen by at least 38% since the start of the Iran conflict, based on open-source analysis and budget data. Reuters reported Tuesday that its sources said those figures broadly aligned with internal U.S. data.

ATACMS and the newer Precision Strike Missile are among the Army's premier long-range precision strike weapons, capable of striking targets hundreds of miles away without putting pilots in harm's way.

ARMY CUTS HELICOPTERS, PUSHES ‘AMAZON FOR WAR’ AS DRONE COMBAT RESHAPES MILITARY

Military planners consider them particularly valuable against heavily defended adversaries because they can destroy command posts, air defenses, logistics hubs and other high-value targets from beyond many enemy air-defense systems.

Patriot and THAAD serve a different mission. Rather than striking enemy targets, they defend U.S. forces and allies by intercepting incoming ballistic missiles, while Tomahawk cruise missiles allow the Navy to conduct long-range strikes from ships and submarines.

The report comes as Pentagon leaders have increasingly warned about the challenge of sustaining prolonged, high-intensity conflicts against major powers while replenishing advanced weapons consumed in combat.

That concern has accelerated efforts to pair expensive precision missiles with far larger numbers of lower-cost, "attritable" drones and autonomous systems that can be produced rapidly and fielded at scale. Officials argue the approach would allow commanders to reserve million-dollar precision weapons for the highest-value targets while relying on less expensive systems for surveillance, electronic warfare and many strike missions.

Military leaders caution, however, that inexpensive drones are not a replacement for long-range precision missiles such as ATACMS and PrSM. Those weapons remain essential for striking hardened command centers, air-defense batteries and other heavily defended targets at distances many lower-cost drones cannot yet reach or survive.

Trump has met repeatedly with executives from the nation's largest defense contractors, pressing them to accelerate production and expand manufacturing capacity as conflicts in Iran and Ukraine strain U.S. stockpiles.

Following a White House meeting in March, Trump said the companies had agreed to quadruple production of what he called "Exquisite Class Weaponry," including some of the military's most advanced missile systems. At a second meeting in June and again at a defense summit in July, the president urged industry leaders to move faster, telling executives, "We have the best quality in the world, but we need a little more speed."

The production push is also reflected in the administration's budget priorities. Trump's proposed $1.5 trillion defense budget would more than triple spending on drones and autonomous systems while boosting investment in munitions production, missile defense and Tomahawk cruise missile procurement.

item.title: Tennessee coach unloads on NCAA's 'bulls–t', after star linebacker suspended for outdated rule
item.description: Josh Heupel called the NCAA's two-game suspension of Arion Carter "bullsh*t," blasting outdated rules after the linebacker returned from the NFL Draft.
item.content:encoded:
KNOXVILLE, TN - After the NCAA decided it was going to suspend Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter for the opening two games of the upcoming season, his head coach did not hesitate to call out the organization for the current rule structure.

Following the 2025 season, Carter decided it was time to pursue his NFL dreams by declaring for the draft and hiring a professional agent to start the process. It was at that moment that the Tennessee linebacker lost his collegiate eligibility according to the antiquated rules currently in place.

Because Carter also accepted a $427 plane ticket from his professional agent to attend a training session, which is when the linebacker first discovered that he had suffered a foot injury that would prevent him from fully reaching his potential of being drafted high.

NCAA ROCKED BY COLORADO JUDGE'S 2022 CLASS ELIGIBILITY RULING THAT COULD RESHAPE COLLEGE SPORTS THIS YEAR

In reality, Arion would have lost millions because of the injury, so he decided the best course of action was a return to college, which transpired just weeks after he first initially announced his decision to go pro.

Carter also paid back the $427 and the school self-reported the 'violation' to the NCAA.

After informing Tennessee that he wanted to return, the question whether the Vols had a roster spot for him. So, he entered the transfer portal for a quick stop, before rejoining the Tennessee football program.

Speaking on Tuesday before the Vols open Fall camp, head coach Josh Heupel did not mince words on the NCAA's punishment of a 2-game suspension for the linebacker.

"He's done everything the right way..The ruling that came out from the NCAA of a 2-game suspension I truly believe is bullshit," Heupel fiercely noted. "You look at the landscape of college football, the rules of NIL and everything, I think the ruling is completely outdated. I am disappointed for him, and for us, with the result of that ruling."

NCAA suspends Tennessee linebacker for $427 plane ticket, as college sports hands out millions in NIL

What did the NCAA have to say in response to upholding a 2-game suspension for Arion Carter?

"NCAA rules are clear: student-athletes may not sign with agents to pursue NFL Draft opportunities, and this student-athlete knowingly violated those longstanding rules. When student-athletes violate NCAA rules, the school declares them ineligible and works with the national office to determine requirements for reinstatement, which can include repayment and/or withholding from competition."

The problem is that there is no way back for an athlete if they decided to declare for the draft, but potentially get hurt in the early training process before all-star games, and also before winter workouts are set to begin in college.

The whole process is laughable when it comes to what is actually transpiring in college athletics right now.

There are schools using agents to circumvent that rev-share cap so athletes can make millions, while high school prospects are signing are agreeing to terms with schools that include private airfare travel for the player themself and their family.

Ted Cruz urges Senate to stay in Washington until Protect College Sports Act passes this week

Right now, college athletes are making millions of dollars for their schools, and the NCAA, but a rule that is outdated is preventing a football player from garnering national exposure like Carter would when Tennessee plays Georgia Tech in a primetime game during the second week.

"AC at the end of last chose to enter his name in the NFL Draft process in the middle of January, right before the deadline where you have to make the final declaration," Josh Heupel noted. "He found out he needed a medical procedure that was gonna require surgery. He made the choice, and the right choice for him, to come back to college football.

"He was upfront and honest, and paid back the four-hundred-dollar flight. He's done everything, and handled everything, the right way. Very truthful, and upfront about everything. I think it's unfortunate that a young man that represents everything inside of this game the right way is faced with that ruling."

Now, even though he is a leader on the Tennessee football team, Arion Carter will miss the opening games of the 2026 season.

The young man could have sued the NCAA, and probably won pretty easily, and this would have been another court case the organization would have had to deal with.

But, Carter is going about his business in preparation for the season and handling it with grace.

There are plenty of people who don't agree with the NCAA upholding a suspension, and the Tennessee administration is high on the list. And most likely, college football fans across the country.

item.title: Trump admin trucking crackdown lands 51 immigration detentions, 36 English language proficiency violations
item.description: Operation Highway Shield resulted in 766 unsafe vehicles placed out of service and 51 immigration detentions as the Trump administration's trucking industry crackdown expands.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump's administration announced the results of a crackdown on illegal immigration in the trucking industry Tuesday.

The Department of Transportation (DOT) began the crackdown, Operation Highway Shield, in Florida earlier this year. The DOT has since expanded the effort to multiple states in the Midwest, including Illinois, Indiana, Iowa and Ohio, Fox News has learned.

Officials carried out 3,487 enforcement stops during the operation that resulted in 766 unsafe commercial vehicles or drivers placed out of service, 51 immigration detentions, 47 criminal charges filed, 39 incarcerations, 36 English language proficiency (ELP) violations and three cargo theft recoveries totaling roughly $1 million in stolen freight.

TRUMP TAPS VETERANS TO FIX ILLEGAL ALIEN TRUCKING PROBLEM PLAGUING US ROADWAYS

The Trump administration maintains that federal immigration and commercial driving enforcement remains a top priority.

Fox News previously broke news about the ramped-up enforcement efforts in Florida in March. Florida troopers said up to half of truckers at some weigh stations cannot meet English proficiency requirements.

"I try to concentrate on the [signs] they have to read," Master Trooper Craig Lents said at the time. "If you are going down the road at 70 miles per hour, and you see that sign, you only see it for a split second."

In another encounter caught on video, a trooper asked a trucker what a road sign meant.

VIRGINIA BUS CRASH THAT KILLED FIVE INVOLVED DRIVER WHO DOESN'T SPEAK ENGLISH, SEAN DUFFY SAYS

The trucker replied, "No."

The trooper then asked what drivers should do if they saw the sign, to which the trucker replied, "No," again.

The Trump administration has noted that federal English requirements have been on the books for years.

"It's been the law for a long period of time," said Derek Barrs, Federal Motor Carrier Safety administrator. "It's a safety issue. … If there was a crash or something like that, I would want to make sure that driver would know how to respond — slow down for upcoming traffic or a crash that has happened up ahead."

ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT TRUCK DRIVER FROM INDIA ARRESTED IN DEADLY CALIFORNIA HIT-AND-RUN AFTER BIDEN RELEASE

Authorities explained that being unable to speak or read English is dangerous because truckers are driving by important road signs at high speeds while carrying hundreds of tons.

The enforcement push comes after a string of deadly crashes nationwide involving drivers the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) claims were in the U.S. illegally or operating with commercial drivers' licenses (CDLs) they should never have had.

item.title: Iran’s unseen supreme leader becomes weapon in escalating power struggle, experts say
item.description: Iran's rival factions invoke Mojtaba Khamenei's name to attack opponents, but his prolonged public absence raises questions about who governs.
item.content:encoded:
Iran’s rival political factions are increasingly invoking the authority of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei to attack their opponents and protect their own positions, even as questions persist over whether he is actively governing the country, according to an Iran expert.

The internal struggle surfaced in two reports published by Iran International concerning Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s relationship with the new supreme leader.

In the first report, senior cleric Mohammad-Bagher Kharrazi, a relative of the Khamenei family by marriage, claimed Pezeshkian had repeatedly threatened to resign and was warned that his next resignation would be accepted.

IRAN EXPERT BRANDS ISLAMIC CENTER OF ENGLAND IRAN'S 'UK OFFICE,' URGES IMMEDIATE CLOSURE

"If he resigns one more time, I will approve it," Kharrazi quoted Khamenei as saying.

Pezeshkian’s office strongly denied the account. Mehdi Tabatabaei, the president’s deputy for communications and information, called the allegation "baseless and an outright lie," while another presidential advisor said Kharrazi had no contact with the supreme leader and was known for telling "strange stories."

Hours later, Iran International published a second report alleging Pezeshkian had met Mojtaba Khamenei only once, inside a vehicle with tinted windows at an undisclosed location in Tehran.

According to the outlet’s unnamed sources, the encounter lasted several minutes, the two men could not see each other and Pezeshkian was not permitted to shake Khamenei’s hand. The report alleged that the president later questioned whether the voice he heard had actually belonged to the supreme leader.

IRAN’S GOOD COP, BAD COP GAME IMPLODES AS EXPERTS WARN REGIME VIEWS US AS 'EVIL'

The claims have not been independently verified. Pezeshkian previously described a substantially different encounter, saying publicly that he had spent approximately two and a half hours with Khamenei in a cordial atmosphere.

Kasra Aarabi, director of IRGC research at United Against Nuclear Iran, said the competing claims surrounding Pezeshkian and Mojtaba Khamenei reflected a deeper struggle inside what he described as an "Islamist oligarchic mafia system."

Under Ali Khamenei, Aarabi said, the supreme leader functioned as the system’s "godfather," arbitrating among rival Islamist factions and guaranteeing their access to power and money. His removal created a vacuum that Mojtaba Khamenei’s appointment was intended to fill, but the new supreme leader’s prolonged public absence has left rival factions uncertain about who is actually in charge.

"The very essence of this mafia system is built on a godfather," Aarabi said. "If the godfather is absent, whether because he is severely incapacitated or nonexistent, that vacuum… re-emerges between the various Islamist oligarchic clans."

Aarabi said those factions are not primarily divided by ideology.

"They’re not competing over ideology," he said. "They’re competing over raw power and economic interests."

In that environment, Aarabi said, Mojtaba Khamenei’s name has become a political instrument that competing factions can invoke to legitimize themselves, constrain their rivals or justify decisions whose true source remains unclear.

WHO IS AHMAD VAHIDI? IRAN’S NEW IRGC CHIEF TIED TO GLOBAL ATTACKS AND ‘DEATH TO AMERICA’ IDEOLOGY

"Mojtaba’s name is the glue that’s holding the system together right now," Aarabi said. "Each of these clans invokes his name to justify its existence, legitimize its position, and consolidate its place within this fragile system."

Exiled Iranian journalist Mehdi Ghadimi described the resignation claims as part of a recurring political strategy used by reformist administrations.

"This is a familiar cycle," Ghadimi said. "Whenever they feel that their usefulness to the supreme leader has come to an end, they start circulating these resignation rumors in an effort to build public sympathy and improve their image before being pushed aside."

Ghadimi said similar rumors surrounded former presidents Mohammad Khatami and Hassan Rouhani during the final years of their administrations. He argued that reformist-aligned media channels often continue circulating resignation claims even after a president’s office formally denies them, allowing officials later to portray themselves as having challenged the supreme leader.

On Mojtaba Khamenei’s status, Ghadimi went further than Aarabi, saying he did not believe there was "a functioning person by that name who is capable of thinking, making decisions or speaking."

"Either he is dead, or he is being kept alive in an extremely unstable and severely deteriorated condition," Ghadimi said.

Aarabi said the two reports illustrate that dynamic. A cleric opposed to or unaligned with Pezeshkian invoked Mojtaba Khamenei’s authority to weaken the president by claiming his next resignation would be accepted, while figures around Pezeshkian pushed back with an account portraying the president as having met directly with the supreme leader.

Mojtaba Khamenei has not appeared in any publicly released video or audio recording since succeeding his father, according to Iran International. Iranian officials have offered conflicting accounts about how often senior government figures have met him.

Aarabi cautioned that using Khamenei’s name as a source of authority will become increasingly difficult if his public absence continues.

"There’s only so many times you can use someone’s name without any proof of life that they actually exist," Aarabi said. "The longer Mojtaba is absent, the more questions develop over whether he is alive or able. And as soon as that doubt increases, you will see this infighting increase."

item.title: Trump keeps calling Thune despite public fight over SAVE America Act
item.description: John Thune says Trump called him twice in one morning, pushing back on reports their working relationship over the SAVE America Act has collapsed.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: The reports of President Donald Trump and Senate Majority Leader John Thune's dead working relationship have been greatly exaggerated, the South Dakota Republican leader told Fox News Digital.

"I've heard from him twice this morning already. He called me over the weekend, and so there, you know, we talk, I don't bother him, I'm not calling him every day," Thune said in an interview.

Last week, Trump said, "We're going to find out," whether Thune was the man for the job to lead Senate Republicans, casting doubt on a critical relationship between him and the Senate’s top Republican.

TRUMP QUESTIONS THUNE'S LEADERSHIP AS SAVE AMERICA ACT STALLS

The tension stems from the SAVE America Act floundering in the Senate, and Trump’s desire to see the election integrity package passed by any means necessary.

Thune doesn’t see Trump’s comment as a personal slight, however. Both he and the president "want to get to the same place. We have, sometimes, disagreements about how best to get there."

"Most of mine are constrained by what's achievable in an institution like the Senate that has procedural roadblocks to do almost anything," Thune said.

"We have those candid conversations, but I'm not worried about that relationship," he continued. "I know he's going to push as hard as he can. That's his business model, is to just keep pushing, pushing, pushing to get people to go as far as they can go."

SENATE FACES 'COME-TO-JESUS' MOMENT ON TRUMP'S ELECTION PRIORITY UNDER GOP'S NEW PLAN

There is a voracious appetite among Trump, Senate Republicans and their base to see the SAVE America Act passed. One that Thune hears every day, either online or within his own conference.

It’s dominated the oxygen inside the Capitol and beyond its walls, and the pressure comes as the Senate is sprinting to finish work on key items, like preventing a government shutdown and confirming dozens of Trump’s nominees.

"There are good days and bad days," Thune said. "And around here, probably lately more bad days than good days, but you know you just kind of, like I said, keep your head down, do the work."

But passing the SAVE America Act is the most elusive item for Republicans, given the current make up of the Senate.

While there are a cohort of Republicans who are voting against it, Thune made the point that every single Senate Democrat has shut it down each of the five times that it’s been brought to the floor in a variety of configurations.

And Thune is one of the Republicans that wants the bill passed — he’s an original co-sponsor of the SAVE Act, the precursor to the current version of the SAVE America Act. The avenue of cutting Democrats out of the equation and ramming through aspects of the bill through budget reconciliation exists, which Thune is interested in pursuing.

But then comes the problem of generating 50 votes to support that, and keeping those votes together to shut down "crazy democratic amendments."

GOP RIFT GROWS AS THUNE HITS BRAKES ON TRUMP'S ELECTION BILL TO AVERT SHUTDOWN

Thune's job helming the Senate majority is to do the math on what can be accomplished in an institution that’s "designed" to be difficult. And the votes still aren’t adding up.

"I keep asking the question, am I the only one in this town that can count to 50? Because it seems like these questions recur and there are a lot of people out there who haven't seemed to internalize the fact that there aren't Democrats that are going to flip and vote for this," Thune said.

"And there aren't 50 Republicans that are going to vote to nuke the filibuster. Those are two facts that are indisputable and unchangeable."

Thune’s position is, by extension, an embodiment of the Senate in many ways.

Unlike the House, legislation and agendas can’t be rammed through without a bipartisan agreement to blast through the filibuster. And senators' concerns and desires encompass an entire state, not just a sliver of a state’s population.

Through several interviews with Fox News Digital, he’s instilled that part of his job is to listen and take consensus on what does and doesn’t work, deliberating on the best path for a deliverable outcome.

"This place was supposed to be difficult, so that no dictator could master it, and I think that's kind of the role of the Senate in our system and our democracy," Thune said.

"It's important to keep that in perspective, but it's frustrating as heck when you're somebody who likes to get things done, likes to get results, and you've got procedural roadblocks holding things up as we try to wind down and get some things done," he continued.

item.title: Vance to host Congress at White House to discuss legislative action on fraud
item.description: Vice President JD Vance will host roughly 20 members of Congress at the White House to discuss legislative action targeting Medicare and Medicaid fraud.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: Vice President JD Vance will host members of Congress at the White House on Wednesday morning for a fraud task force meeting where members will discuss potential legislative action to address the administration’s crackdown on fraud.

A source familiar with the meeting told Fox News Digital that roughly 20 members from both the House and Senate are expected at the meeting. Vance will also detail how members can target fraud in the various states and districts they represent.

Vance has previously hosted meetings at the White House to address fraud with a number of attorneys general alongside other members of the administration involved in the task force led by Vance.

PENNSYLVANIA AG EXPLAINS WHY STATE LEADS NATION IN MEDICAID FRAUD CONVICTIONS WHILE OTHERS BATTLE MASS SCHEMES

"Our task force is using every tool at its disposal to end fraud once and for all. "President Trump, Vice President Vance, and all of the task force’s interagency partners will not relent until every fraudster is brought to justice."

On Tuesday, the Justice Department announced that it is expanding its Northeast Health Care Fraud Strike Force to Philadelphia as federal and state authorities target alleged Medicare and Medicaid fraud involving home healthcare services, adding Pennsylvania to a number of states across the country where the administration is honed in on fraud.

Federal and state law enforcement charged 19 defendants accused of participating in schemes involving more than $4 million in claims submitted to Medicare and Medicaid, according to a DOJ release obtained by Fox News.

On Sunday, Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday also announced a plea agreement involving the final defendant in a previously charged 21-defendant case tied to more than $1.7 million in claims.

"The vice president’s task force continues to stop the flow of taxpayer funds before they fall into the hands of fraudsters and deliver savings to the American people," a spokesperson for Vance told Fox News Digital. "This is great momentum in the fight for the President’s War on Fraud."

WATCH: DR. OZ SAYS NEWSOM, OTHER BLUE STATES HAVE TURNED MEDICAID FRAUD INTO A 'FEATURE'

The task force has suspended payments to a number of healthcare providers who have been suspected of fraud across the country. In June, the Trump administration revealed new figures that show a drastic 7,100% spike in Medicare claims for skin substitutes in just six years, surging from $200 million to $14.4 billion from 2019 to 2025.

CMS identified 4,200 suspicious claims for skin substitutes, known as allografts, totaling $224 million in charges through May of this year.

"That's a lot of money," Oz said during a news conference in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on Wednesday. "And that bankrupts not just hospital systems and physician groups, but it causes major problems across the entire landscape."

FEDERAL GOVERNMENT’S LANDLORD JOINS VANCE FRAUD CRACKDOWN AS WHITE HOUSE WIDENS HUNT: 'CRITICAL FORCE'

"Vice President JD Vance and Republicans are doing a great job hunting down Fraud in the various States," Trump posted on Truth Social in June. "Billions of Dollars is being found, and we've just started!"

item.title: Wisconsin brewery that promised free beer when Trump dies now plans 'half-price beer day' when McConnell dies
item.description: Minocqua Brewing Company announced half-price beer when Sen. Mitch McConnell dies, blaming the Kentucky Republican for half of America's problems.
item.content:encoded:
The Wisconsin brewery that previously sparked outrage by promising free beer on "the day" President Donald Trump dies is once again drawing criticism after announcing plans for a "half-price beer day" when Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., dies.

In a post on Instagram on Monday, Minocqua Brewing Company said it plans to celebrate McConnell's death by offering beer at half price, arguing the longtime Kentucky Republican was responsible for "about half of all America's current problems."

"Well, folks, if our logic is right, we're supposed to get the news today that ‘Rigor Tortoise’ kicked the bucket about two months ago," the brewery said.

'THIS IS NOT NORMAL': AOC UNLOADS ON MCCONNELL'S PROLONGED ABSENCE

"Why today? Because so-called 'Establishment Democratic Hero' and modern day gutless member of the do-nothing opposition party — Governor Andy Beshear — failed to call a special election to replace the ‘ghost from Kentucky’ before August 3rd — which means by Kentucky law, the seat will go unfilled until January."

"When they announce that McConnell's Faustian dance has finally ended, we're gonna start serving our beer at ‘half price,’ because we promised #halfpricebeerday on the day they unplug the ventilator," the brewery continued.

McConnell, who is 84, has not been in the Senate for more than a month after being hospitalized for a fall in his home.

Last week, Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear demanded that McConnell prove he is fit to continue serving in Congress after a lengthy hospital stay or resign from office.

"I am calling on you to directly and verbally address the people of Kentucky and provide proof of your capacity to serve, or resign," Beshear wrote in a letter to McConnell, obtained by Fox News Digital.

WISCONSIN DEM'S BAR LAMENTS 'WE ALMOST GOT FREE BEER DAY' FOR TRUMP ASSASSINATION

In the post, the brewery said it chose the name "half-price beer day" because it blamed McConnell for "about half" of the country's current problems while noting that its previously announced "free beer day" promotion remained reserved for "someone more special."

The brewery also promoted "half-price beer day" T-shirts and encouraged supporters to wear them when the event eventually takes place.

Minocqua Brewing Company, which in a January social media post appeared to suggest it would give free beer to patrons if Trump was killed, while not explicitly using his name, is currently fighting getting their permit revoked.

The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reported on July 27 that Wisconsin's Department of Revenue sent a notice to liberal activist and brewery owner Kirk Bangstad announcing plans to revoke the brewery’s permit.

'FREE BEER' FOR TRUMP DEATH DEM ACTIVIST RUNNING FOR WISCONSIN GOV: 'I WILL WIN' IF THEY SILENCE ME

The Sentinel reported that state regulators pursued revoking Bangstad's alcohol license after authorities seized canned beer from his company in June, alleging it had been transported from Illinois without the required permits and taxes. The paper also reported that Bangstad criticized the proposed action as an excessive response, arguing the alleged tax violations did not warrant shutting down his business.

The revocation of the beer permit was set to go into effect on Tuesday, but a spokesperson for Wisconsin's Department of Revenue told Fox News Digital in a statement that "Minocqua Brewing Company has filed an administrative appeal, and, therefore, the permit will not be revoked, pending the outcome of the administrative appeal."

Bangstad, the owner of the brewery, is also the founder of the Minocqua Brewing Company SuperPAC, which "aims to remove Republican federal and state elected officials who perpetuated the election lies that caused the Insurrection of January 6, 2021, and whose downplaying of the seriousness of COVID-19 caused so many unnecessary deaths in our country," according to the brewery’s website.

Fox News Digital reached out to Minocqua Brewing Company, Gov. Beshear's office and Sen. McConnell's office for comment but did not immediately receive responses.

NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM DEMANDS RELEASED BY PIMA COUNTY SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT IN BID TO IDENTIFY SENDER

item.title: Embattled GOP rep takes dramatic step to 'clear my name' as abuse allegations engulf House race
item.description: Rep. Max Miller filed for an ethics investigation into himself to clear his name as Sen. Bernie Moreno calls him a "danger" to his own family.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Max Miller, R-Ohio, is calling for an investigation into abuse allegations made against him by his ex-wife, as the dramatic family feud overshadows his race for re-election.

Miller has consistently denied wrongdoing and accused both his ex-wife and her father, Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, of trying to take down his political career.

"In light of all the renewed interest in my family affairs, I am going to file my own paperwork for an ethics investigation into myself to clear my name from these horrific attacks on myself and my family. I have absolutely nothing to hide," Miller wrote on X on Tuesday.

"We will be providing the committee all necessary documents needed for a detail examination. The accusations continue to change, but my facts stay the same. I am looking forward to my colleagues reading everything for themselves."

OHIO GOP FAMILY FEUD EXPLODES AS SEN BERNIE MORENO CALLS ON REP MAX MILLER TO RESIGN

The Ethics Committee confirmed on Tuesday afternoon that it would investigate allegations that Miller "may have engaged in domestic violence and abuse or illegal drug use."

Emily Moreno, who filed for divorce from Miller in 2024 after two years of marriage, has accused him of physically abusing both her and their young daughter. Allegations include that he scalded Moreno with boiling water and held a gun to her head during two separate occasions, and that she had to get their daughter medical aid for a broken collar bone after she was in Miller's care.

Miller suggested in a livestream on X over the weekend that Moreno had suffered from mental health issues in the past and that might be the reason behind her accusations. He also said none of the allegations she made have been substantiated by relevant entities.

"Every single one of these allegations were already investigated. No criminal charge has ever been filed against me," Miller said in the video. He said the water incident occurred during "horseplay" between the two, and disputed that the water was boiling. He also said Moreno took their daughter to the emergency room thinking there was a bruise on their daughter's neck, but that the mark was from finger painting.

SEN BERNIE MORENO CALLS FOR EX-SON-IN-LAW TO RESIGN FROM HOUSE, GET 'SERIOUS PSYCHOLOGICAL HELP'

But mounting public pressure has brought the Cleveland-area feud to Washington, where Sen. Moreno told reporters Tuesday that Miller "fails to meet that minimum basic standard" for elected officials who get to serve.

He also criticized Miller in a statement posted on X, calling him a "danger" to his daughter and granddaughter. Miller and Moreno share custody over the child.

The intense public scrutiny is also potentially putting Miller's re-election into question, with Democrats seeing new opportunity in what was a relatively safe red seat in the Cleveland suburbs.

One House GOP source, who was granted anonymity to speak candidly about a sensitive situation, told Fox News Digital the situation was a "f—-ing trainwreck."

DEMOCRATS TARGET MORE GOP HOUSE SEATS AFTER SOCIALIST VICTORIES ROCK LEFT-WING PRIMARIES

The source noted that the allegations against Miller had not been substantiated, but said "the court of public opinion is a b—-."

Miller likely appears to voters to have "a little too much on his plate," the source said.

Meanwhile, a House Republican, who was granted anonymity to speak candidly, said Miller should not run for re-election. "We must lead by example," they said.

The same House Republican also called for Reps. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., and Cory Mills, R-Fla., also facing harassment allegations that they have denied, to similarly drop out of their races.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

But Miller has been defiant so far, expressing confidence that he'll win in November.

The House Ethics Committee, which Miller is calling on to investigate his case, recently recommended that Edwards be censured for his behavior toward two young female staffers.

item.title: Devastated mother blames soft-on-crime policies after career criminal is charged in son’s death
item.description: Jacob Freytes' family pushes for mandatory life sentences for child killers after the 12-year-old was fatally struck by a stray bullet in the Bronx.
item.content:encoded:
The family of a 12-year-old boy killed by a stray bullet in the Bronx is demanding change after a suspect with a lengthy arrest record was charged with his murder.

After the death of Jacob Freytes, the son of a retired NYPD detective sergeant, his mother and sister are pushing for "Jacob's Law," which they say would require life sentences for people convicted of recklessly taking a child's life.

"I gave him a kiss, and I walked out, and we always do a little dolphin kiss. And I walked out and went to work," Migdalia Martinez, Freytes' mother, told "Fox & Friends" Tuesday.

2 DETAINED AFTER SHOOTING IN NEW YORK LEAVES 15-YEAR-OLD KILLED, TWO OTHERS WOUNDED: POLICE

"Around five o'clock, they called me and said that he had gotten shot. And all I could do was try to think of different ways to get here faster," she added. "When I got there, I just seen my boy gone."

Freytes, who was riding his bike to a nearby bodega to buy a ball, was shot and killed after a suspect opened fire during an alleged street dispute. Two other adults were also wounded in the shooting.

Police said William Ferrer, 45, was arrested and faces multiple charges, including second-degree murder. He has pleaded not guilty. Ferrer has an arrest record dating back more than 25 years, including prior charges for drunk driving, drug possession, menacing and criminal contempt, according to the New York Post.

New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch addressed Ferrer’s arrest on X, writing, "Jacob was an innocent bystander on his bike when he was taken from his family yesterday in an act of senseless gun violence.

HOUSE DEMOCRAT BLASTED AFTER EARLY RELEASE LAW FREED INMATES LATER CHARGED WITH MURDER

"No arrest can ever ease the pain of this unimaginable loss, but the NYPD will continue to do everything in our power to seek justice for Jacob."

The family is calling for a proposed "Jacob's Law" that they say would require life sentences for people convicted of recklessly taking a child’s life. The family also criticized New York's crime policies, including cash bail reforms for misdemeanors and the end of stop-and-frisk.

"It's just so much that they allow that, at this point, it's just safer more for the criminals than it is for hardworking people," Martinez said.

Freytes’ sister, Angelica Coriano, said the family welcomed the charges but remained uneasy about whether the suspect would receive enough prison time if convicted.

LOUISIANA BILL EXPANDS FIRST-DEGREE MURDER CHARGES AND DEATH PENALTY ELIGIBILITY AFTER MALL SHOOTING

"'Jacob's Law' will allow for there to be no in-between whether somebody goes to jail or not for taking a child's life recklessly. It'll allow for criminals to go straight to jail or prison instead of the family having to go to court continuously hoping and wondering if they're [going to] get the justice that they deserve for the child that they lost," Coriano said.

"And we went to court and found out all the charges that he'd be receiving, which is great, but we still have to sit with the worry whether he'll face all the time that is necessary enough to keep him where he needs to be. And that type of uncertainty is very uncomfortable for us as a family, knowing that we'll never see our child again."

Martinez remembered her son as a "funny, quirky kid" who loved his friends, family and playing video games. 

"There wasn't an old woman he didn't help with bags or cross the street," she said. "There wasn't a person that if he caught your eye, he'd make sure to tell you hi."

Angel Reese just wrapped up an extraordinary 10-day stretch that most young girls in America could only dream about.

On July 24, Mattel unveiled a Barbie doll made in her likeness. The doll wore a pink jersey featuring Reese’s No. 5, the number she wears with the Atlanta Dream, and included details such as her headband, leg sleeve, necklace, pink nails and signature Reebok shoes.

On July 25, she competed in her third consecutive WNBA All-Star Game.

On Aug. 3, a matching Barbie edition of the Angel Reese 1, her signature sneaker, went on sale.

WNBA COMMISSIONER VOWS TO CRACK DOWN ON 'RACISM, MISOGYNY,' DODGES BIG QUESTIONS AT ALL-STAR PRESS CONFERENCE

That same night, the Dream held "Barbie Game Day" at State Farm Arena, complete with special ticket packages and limited-edition merchandise. Reese’s doll sat beside her during media availability.

In 10 days, Reese received her own Barbie, a matching version of her signature shoe and an entire WNBA promotional event tied to the collaboration.

Yet even that wasn’t enough to keep Reese from returning to her favorite subject: what the world had denied her.

"Honestly, I didn’t have a lot of dolls because I didn’t have dolls that really looked like me much," Reese said when asked what dolls she played with growing up.

"That’s why I kind of really wanted to make sure this was super intentional, because now that they have a doll that looks like you, nails and hair, but also you can be a killer on the court as well."

Reese didn’t say Black dolls never existed, but she clearly framed her childhood doll options as a failure of representation.

So, it's worth noting that Mattel introduced Christie, a Black character in Barbie’s world, in 1968. The first doll officially named Black Barbie arrived in 1980, more than two decades before Reese was born. American Girl introduced Addy Walker in 1993.

And in 1998, Mattel sold officially licensed African-American NBA Barbie dolls wearing authentic team uniforms and packaged with basketballs.

That was four years before Reese was born, meaning that a Black basketball-playing Barbie existed before Angel Reese did. Somehow, that didn't qualify as a doll that "looked like her" and could be a "killer on the court."

Her new doll doesn't mark the arrival of representation that had never existed. It marks another lucrative commercial opportunity for one of the most heavily promoted athletes in women’s sports.

Last month, I wrote about how frequently Reese presents herself as overlooked or unfairly treated, even as attention has helped make her one of the most famous and commercially successful players in women’s basketball.

ANGEL REESE’S LATEST WNBA CONTROVERSY SHOWS HOW VICTIMHOOD BECAME CENTRAL TO HER BRAND

Here's the truth: Angel Reese is incredibly privileged.

Reese attended St. Frances Academy in Baltimore, a private school where high school tuition is currently $15,000 per year. She was a McDonald's All-American and one of the top college recruits in the country.

She then played basketball at Maryland before transferring to LSU on a full scholarship, earning a free four-year college education and a bachelor's degree in Interdisciplinary Studies.

Now, she's a professional athlete with major endorsements, millions of social-media followers, a podcast, a signature shoe and a Barbie doll. She walked in the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show and attended the Met Gala for the third consecutive year in May.

And the preferential treatment hasn’t been limited to corporate America.

WNBA FANS CALL OUT GLARING DOUBLE STANDARD AFTER ANGEL REESE’S CLUELESS RESPONSE TO PAIGE BUECKERS BET

The Dream acquired Reese from Chicago in April for two first-round picks. The deal came only months after Reese publicly ripped the Sky’s roster, questioned her teammates and warned that she might have to "move in a different direction" if the organization didn’t improve.

Chicago suspended her for comments it deemed "detrimental to the team."

Yet, rather than suffer any real consequence for publicly bashing the organization that drafted her in the first round of the 2024 WNBA Draft, Reese landed with a ready-made contender willing to pay a premium price.

That team then made her the centerpiece of a major marketing campaign, including an entire game-night promotion built around her personal brand.

Most athletes never receive any one of those opportunities, let alone all of them.

Yet, sitting beside a doll made in her image during a night built around celebrating her brand, Reese focused on what the world had failed to give her.

At this point, victimhood no longer seems like an occasional theme in the Angel Reese story.

It looks like the brand.

item.title: Mets call up pitcher known for his over the top strikeout celebrations as dismal season hits new level
item.description: Mets pitcher Jefry Yan does splits and screams after every strikeout in the minors, and his dominant ERA earned him a reported call-up to the MLB.
item.content:encoded:
The New York Mets very comfortably occupy the basement of the National League East and are set to miss the postseason for the second consecutive year. A franchise living in that reality making a roster move would not garner any attention, but when that move involves a guy who does the splits after striking out hitters, an exception is made.

The Mets selected the contract of left-handed pitcher Jefry Yan on July 2, and hours after the MLB trade deadline officially passed on Aug. 3, Yan was among a handful of pitchers reportedly promoted.

Mets fans have nothing to look forward to in the immediate term, but watching Yan potentially make his debut in The Show may as well be appointment viewing.

BREWERS PITCHER ABNER URIBE APOLOGIZES AFTER CONTROVERSIAL STRIKEOUT CELEBRATION SPARKS BACKLASH

Beyond the 29-year-old's impressive numbers at both the AA and AAA levels in 2026, Yan puts on a show, in the most literal way, every time he takes the bump.

Jumping into the air, doing the splits, screaming at the top of his lungs, smacking the ground. You name it, Yan does it.

While his antics look like something straight out of a Savannah Bananas game, the dude can throw a baseball.

After bouncing around the Minor League systems of the Los Angeles Angels, Miami Marlins, and Colorado Rockies early in his career, Yan inked a deal with the Mets in August 2025, and 2026 has been a mighty kind year for the Dominican native.

In 26.2 innings of work with AA Binghamton, Yan posted a 3.71 ERA while striking out 45 batters. After taking the step up to AAA Syracuse, his stuff only got better.

In his 15.0 innings with Syracuse, Yan owns a record of 2-1, an ERA of 2.40 while giving up just six hits and striking out 32.

Do the jokes write themselves given that Yan plays for the punching bag of Major League Baseball? Yes. Will the Mets get clowned on social media when Yan gives up a home run or struggles after doing a Michael Jackson stunt on the mound? You bet.

On the flip side, at least Mets fans have something to talk about for a brief moment other than the team being 19 games below .500 in early August.

item.title: Tick-borne 'rabbit fever' spreads with cases reported near major metro area
item.description: Three probable tularemia cases on Long Island have officials warning residents about the tick-borne illness after a 9-year-old developed severe symptoms.
item.content:encoded:
Health officials on Long Island are warning residents about a rare but potentially serious tick-borne illness.

Three probable cases of tularemia — also known as "rabbit fever" — have been confirmed by the Suffolk County Department of Health Services (SCDHS).

"SCDHS currently has three probable cases of tularemia this year," the agency said in a statement provided to local outlets. "Confirmation of a tularemia diagnosis requires a combination of laboratory testing and fulfillment of specific clinical or epidemiologic criteria. The laboratory testing to confirm a tularemia diagnosis may take several weeks."

NO CURE, NO VACCINE: EXPERTS WARN OF RARE BOURBON VIRUS AFTER FIRST NY CASE

One case involved a 9-year-old patient who was bitten by a tick while playing outside, according to NBC4 New York. After the tick was removed, he later developed high fever, severe head and neck pain, swollen lymph nodes/glands, body aches and extreme fatigue.

After multiple doctor visits and nearly a month of illness, an infectious disease specialist diagnosed the boy with tularemia.

Although the family's yard is home to wild rabbits, the patient's mother said he never handled the animals. Doctors believe infected ticks likely fed on the rabbits before biting the boy, transmitting the bacteria, according to reports.

Caused by the bacteria Francisella tularensis, the disease commonly infects rabbits, hares and rodents. However, it is zoonotic, which means it can spread from animals to humans.

The bacteria is a "tier-1 select agent," a classification given to agents and toxins that "present the greatest risk of deliberate misuse with significant potential for mass casualties or devastating effects to the economy, critical infrastructure or public confidence, and pose a severe threat to public health and safety," per the CDC.

TICK BITE ER VISITS HIT HIGHEST SEASONAL LEVEL IN YEARS AS DOCTORS WARN OF DISEASE SURGE

Although tularemia remains rare, with 196 U.S. cases reported in 2023, the disease has become more common in recent years. CDC surveillance found 2,462 cases between 2011 and 2022 — a 56% increase in incidence compared with the previous decade (2001–2010).

Daniel Ruderfer, M.D., chief of the Division of Pediatric Infectious Diseases at Hackensack Meridian K. Hovnanian Children's Hospital in New Jersey, believes that the increase in cases is mostly due to improved microbiology detection methods.

"The traditional method of confirming cases has historically been via growth in culture and antibody testing," he previously told Fox News Digital.

"However, newer detection methods, such as PCR testing, are likely a major contributor to the increase in reported cases."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Humans can contract the disease through bites from deer flies or ticks, contact with infected animals, or exposure to contaminated water or aerosols, the same source stated.

Symptoms of tularemia can vary depending on the type of disease. General symptoms include chills, headache, malaise, fatigue, anorexia, myalgia, chest discomfort, cough, severe sore throat, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain, according to Ruderfer.

"Depending on the location of the infected bit or scratch, people can develop localized lymphadenopathy (enlarged lymph nodes) and a cutaneous ulcer at the infection site," he said.

"Other manifestations include conjunctivitis, pneumonia and potentially even bloodstream infections."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The death rate from the disease is typically low, less than 2%, but the CDC noted that it can be as high as 24% in rare, severe cases.

Tularemia can be treated with antibiotics, but no vaccine is currently available.

"The infection is absolutely dangerous and potentially life-threatening if not treated with appropriate antibiotics," said Ruderfer.

Those most at risk include children between 5 and 9 years of age, older men, American Indian and Alaskan Native people, and those living in central U.S. states, according to the report.

The general population is not at an "obvious" risk for infection unless they come into physical contact with an infected rabbit, tick or deer fly, the expert noted.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Those who hunt or interact routinely with rabbits should see a doctor if they develop any concerning symptoms, he advised.

"Many factors might contribute to the higher risk for tularemia in this population, including the concentration of Native American reservations in central states and sociocultural or occupational activities that might increase contact with infected wildlife or arthropods," the CDC wrote.

item.title: WNBA fan goes viral for half-court shot horror show that left him sprawled on the court
item.description: A Portland Fire fan's half-court shot attempt during the WNBA game against the Los Angeles Sparks barely cleared the free throw line area.
item.content:encoded:
Few things in sports can get a fan's nerves up like being told you get to take a half-court shot at an NBA or WNBA game for cash or a car.

Sure, you could, by some miracle, make the shot, but you're more likely to embarrass yourself in front of an arena full of people... at least the ones who are still in their seats and aren't in line for a beer or the bathroom.

But, at least we can all be sure that if you take a shot, the odds of it being a worse display than one put on by a Portland Fire fan over the weekend are very, very low.

WNBA COMMISSIONER CATHY ENGELBERT CAUGHT HITTING LAUGHABLY BAD GOLF SHOT AFTER ALLEGEDLY DITCHING INTERVIEW

The Fire (whose logo I only just realized is a flaming rose. Seriously, I've had an easier time decoding death metal band logos) have a half-court shot competition according to their website. It's sponsored by Toyota, meaning that draining the shot earns you a brand new Toyota.

Hopefully a Land Cruiser. Those are cool.

One fan got this golden opportunity on Sunday when the Fire took on the Los Angeles Sparks and... well, let's just say that Portland area Toyota dealers were not sweating it on this one.

Oh, dear God...

ATLANTA BRAVES FAN TAUNTS THE FREEZE WITH A BLOWN KISS AND GETS PASSED IN SPECTACULAR FASHION

Rule No. 1 of half-court shots should be that whatever you do, your biggest goal is to at least hit the backboard. I'd argue it's much better to airmail that ball into the club level seats than it is to barely get it past the free throw line.

That's a rough look as it is, but imagine putting every last drop of mustard you have on the ball to the point that you go scrawling across that flaming rose logo (seriously, did anyone else not pick up on that at first?). That tells the entire crowd in attendance you gave it your all... which is normally good, but that's not enough "all."

The big winner in all of this is that guy's glasses. Talk about a snug fit. Those things were on there!

That was maybe the only thing that went right for him. If those specs had gone clattering across the hardwood, I think he would've had to change his name, move out of Portland, and start rooting for a new WNBA team.

Luckily for him, he wasn't the only loser as the Fire fell to the Sparks that night 106-101.

item.title: French trans phenom Julie Tétart looks WNBA-ready — so why hasn’t the ‘inclusive’ league called?
item.description: Julie Tétart dominated French women's basketball with 21 points and 20 rebounds per game and says a WNBA call would mean time to talk business.
item.content:encoded:
French trans basketball player Julie Tétart is waiting for a call from one of the inclusive WNBA teams who needs a 6'3 scoring and rebounding machine.

During the 2025-26 season for a club team in Monaco, Tétart dominated the second-tier French women's basketball Ligue 2 by dropping 21 points per game while grabbing 20 rebounds. The biological male, who came out as trans in October 2021, led the league in both categories. It was as season unlike any the Ligue 2 had ever seen.

With those numbers, the WNBA should be knocking down Tétart's door, right?

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SPEAKS OUT TO PROTECT GIRLS AS WNBA ALL-STAR INITIATIVE BACKS ‘GENDER-EXPANSIVE’ GROUP

"If they contact me, I won't say no. But you have to be realistic: I'm old, and there are far better players than me!" the overly humble 34-year-old Tétart told OutKick in French over Instagram direct messages on Monday.

Far better? Are you sure?

Tétart's season was so dominant that French media was stunned when the shredded center didn't win league MVP honors. The season was still good enough to win Player of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year and Domestic Player of the Year.

Woke WNBA fans swear there's no clear and present trans danger to biological women. They swear this is some sort of delusion cooked up by MAGA.

RILEY GAINES SAYS WNBA IS 'HELLBENT' ON BEING AN ACTIVIST ORGANIZATION OVER A BASKETBALL LEAGUE

Meanwhile, Tétart destroyed Ligue 2 so badly that there were collusion allegations being made against league captains and coaches who voted on the MVP award.

Those same voters are alleged to have excluded 43-year-old trans player Aurore Pautou (14.4 PPG, 7.7 RPG) from winning postseason awards. French trans groups are furious. "Despite top-tier athletic performance on the court during the 2025/2026 season by Julie and Aurore, voters for the Ligue 2 Féminine de Basket Awards deliberately decided not to grant them any awards," activist group TRANSpire cried on Instagram.

Former WNBA player Audrey Sauret, who's French, spoke out in April after the MVP drama and sounded a warning to leagues around the world as to what's coming if they don't protect biological females.

"Ligue 2 serves as a kind of testing ground, to introduce trendy ideas, but by allowing them to participate in professional competitions, we create unfair competition, especially for younger players," Sauret wrote. "This can close doors and discourage aspiring athletes. This situation risks becoming commonplace, even if it’s regulated. Men and women aren’t built the same way. Changing hormones doesn’t erase gender differences. I regret that this issue wasn’t addressed much sooner."

TRANS ATHLETE WINS NEW YORK STATE GIRLS' SHOT PUT TITLE, BEATING SECOND PLACE BY MORE THAN 2 FEET

During a March game that should've been a trans showdown, Tétart had 21 points and 30 rebounds, which was a new league record, breaking the previous record of 25 rebounds (Tétart held that record, as well), but Pautou didn't play.

The question we had for Tétart was simple: Would you ever consider trying out for the inclusive WNBA? The trans scoring and rebounding machine seemed confused at first before realizing we were 100% serious.

"Obviously, it's a childhood dream just like for any female basketball player, but unfortunately, it's not possible," the French native wrote back.

Wait a minute, why not? The WNBA is inclusive. What are we missing here?

WNBA COMMISSIONER VOWS TO CRACK DOWN ON 'RACISM, MISOGYNY,' DODGES BIG QUESTIONS AT ALL-STAR PRESS CONFERENCE

"The league, yes. The country, no, haha," Tétart fired back while hinting at some sort of problem with Donald Trump's presidency.

When pressed on what would need to change politically in the U.S., Tétart stopped playing games with me, finally admitting that if a WNBA call came, it would be time to talk business: "I won't say no."

As for Sophie Cunningham's stance that biological males need to stay out of women's sports, I gave Tétart a chance to respond. "Aucun," the French stat stuffer replied.

Translation: "None."

Imagine a Tétart vs. Cunningham matchup in 2027. It's time for the WNBA to once and for all prove just how inclusive it is. Tétart's DMs are wide open.

item.title: Commanders cornerback Ahkello Witherspoon retires from football at 31
item.description: Washington Commanders cornerback Akhello Witherspoon announced his retirement from the NFL at 31 years old. He played for nine seasons after being drafted out of Colorado.
item.content:encoded:
Washington Commanders cornerback Ahkello Witherspoon is retiring from the NFL at 31 years old.

The team announced Tuesday that they placed Witherspoon on the Reserve/Retired List and signed cornerback Fabian Moreau to take his place. Witherspoon practiced Monday and informed the team Tuesday morning that he was retiring, according to ESPN.

Witherspoon signed a one-year, $1.41 million contract with the Commanders in May but will not suit up for them this fall.

Witherspoon played college football at Colorado, where he starred as a defensive back. In 37 games, he recorded 71 tackles, three interceptions, 27 passes defended, one fumble recovery and one forced fumble.

In his senior year, Witherspoon led Division I college football with 22 passes defended. The San Francisco 49ers selected him in the third round of the 2017 NFL Draft, and he became a key piece in their secondary.
